# Buffered lists have no example and no real-scroll coverage

## Context

Split out of `#17878` per `pull-request-workflow.md` §9.1 — that ticket investigates a reported scroll jump and remains open; this one is the coverage and example gap the investigation exposed, which is deliverable on its own and is not contingent on the outcome.

`Neo.list.Buffered` currently has:

- **no example app.** Measured: **0** files under `examples/` import `list/Buffered`, against a control of **3** for `list/Base`. Nothing under `src/` references it either, apart from `Buffered.mjs` itself — its only consumers live outside this repository.
- **no coverage that can observe a real scroll.** `test/playwright/unit/list/Buffered.spec.mjs` calls `onScrollCapture()` with already-decided absolute `scrollTop` values (80, 40, 205, …). Every `page.mouse.wheel` in the e2e tier moves a single large delta (500, 900, 1500, 4000) and asserts only that scrolling occurred.

## The Problem

The two gaps compound. A component with no example gives scroll-behaviour work nothing to point a browser at — which is exactly what `#17878` hit. And coverage that injects a decided `scrollTop` asserts what the list does with a number it is handed, never what happens to the number across a real scroll, so wheel-distance fidelity can regress while the suite stays green.

`bufferRowRange` and `itemHeight` are the two configs whose whole effect is windowing behaviour, and neither is observable in a test that supplies the scroll position itself.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/list/Buffered.mjs` — `onScrollCapture` (`:695-707`), `calculateMountedRange` (`:314-335`), `createItems` (`:344`), spacer construction (`:445-458`)
- `src/list/Base.mjs:92` — `itemHeight_` defaults to `null`; a fixture omitting it divides `scrollTop` by `null`
- `test/playwright/playwright.config.component.mjs` — the tier that renders its own checkout on a free port, which is what makes a real-browser scroll witness trustworthy here
- `test/playwright/component/apps/` — the tier's per-scenario harness-app convention (`empty-viewport`, `dock-splitter`, `dock-rail`)

## The Fix

- `examples/list/buffered/` — a `Neo.list.Buffered` over 5,000 records with `bufferRowRange`, `itemHeight` and `height` exposed as live config controls, following the `examples/list/base` shape.
- `test/playwright/component/apps/buffered-list/` — a harness app with pinned geometry, following the tier's existing per-scenario convention.
- `test/playwright/component/list/BufferedWheelFidelity.spec.mjs` — real `page.mouse.wheel` gestures, asserting physical DOM `scrollTop`, App-Worker `scrollTop`, `mountedRange` and pool identity in the same run, with a RED CONTROL that drives the same path with a viewport-sized delta so the greens are falsifiable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `examples/list/buffered/` exists and boots, exposing `bufferRowRange` / `itemHeight` / `height` as live controls
- [ ] A component-tier spec drives **incremental** wheel deltas and asserts the scroll seat moves by exactly their sum
- [ ] The spec asserts App-Worker `scrollTop` against the physical DOM seat in the same run
- [ ] The spec covers a mounted-range boundary crossing at a **derived** offset, not an approximate one
- [ ] Negative deltas are covered — reversal lands on the same pixels
- [ ] A RED CONTROL proves the fidelity assertion can fail, and drives the same code path as the green arms rather than writing the scroll seat directly
- [ ] Pool identity is asserted with spacers excluded **by class**, and the spacer count asserted, so the exclusion is proven non-empty

### Transferred from `#17878`

> Received 2026-08-31 under RA-1 on PR #17944. `#17878` reduced to a browser scroll-anchoring defect
> with a one-property Engine repair, and could not close over evidence living in this lane's unmerged
> PR. These three describe **instrument breadth**, which is what this ticket is for. Restated verbatim
> so the transfer loses nothing; they are required here and are **not** discharged by `#17944`.

- [ ] Positive **and negative** small wheel deltas remain incremental before a mounted-range boundary. *(`#17878` retains the positive direction; the negative direction is this lane's.)*
- [ ] DOM `scrollTop` and App-Worker `scrollTop` converge after each gesture without programmatic snap-back.
- [ ] The physical component pool stays bounded and retains its component identities across the boundary.

## Out of Scope

- `#17878`'s reported jump. This ticket delivers the instrument; it does not explain the report, and a green witness does not close that ticket.
- Any change to `src/list/Buffered.mjs`. The `createItems`-on-every-scroll discrepancy is real and stays with `#17878`.
- The programmatic-`scrollTop` entry path, which the wheel arms do not cover.

## Avoided Traps

- **A control that writes the scroll seat directly.** The first revision did, and raced `createItems()`'s re-stamp (`Buffered.mjs:377`) — intermittent, and its failure mode was indistinguishable from the defect it existed to detect.
- **Treating concurrent Playwright runs as independent.** They share ports and servers; a result from a run whose served tree cannot be established is not a result.
- **`slice(1, -1)` for the pool.** Correct today and silent tomorrow — the spacers are excluded by class so the reason is in the code.
